html:
King of England from 1509 to 1547, remembered for his six marriages and for breaking with the pope to make himself head of the Church of England.

His first wife, Catherine of Aragon, daughter of Isabella of Castile, gave him a daughter, Mary, but no surviving son. Henry wanted to marry Anne Boleyn and asked the pope to annul his marriage. The pope, under the sway of Catherine's nephew, the emperor Charles V, refused. So Henry and Parliament broke with Rome, and the Act of Supremacy of 1534 made the king supreme head of the church in England.

His six wives:

  • Catherine of Aragon: marriage annulled;
  • Anne Boleyn: beheaded;
  • Jane Seymour: died after giving birth to his son Edward;
  • Anne of Cleves: marriage annulled;
  • Catherine Howard: beheaded;
  • Catherine Parr: outlived him.

From 1536 he dissolved the monasteries and sold their lands. Henry was no follower of Luther, but his break opened the way for Protestants, and his daughter Elizabeth I settled the Church of England.
